summary: Lane County, OR ground cabin on Bearbones Mountain, dated 1933 or 1934 (style disputed), briefly staffed in 1935 and gone by 1964; no current site report found.

facts.design: Ground cabin; sources disagree (L-5, L-6, or a plan FC-2 10 x 10 ground house)
facts.status_note: Gone by 1964 per the register and firelookout.com; no source describes what remains on the summit

visit.trail_note: A 1953 survey description gives directions ending at a trail up the mountain; no current access report found

events.note: Forest Lookouts: a plan FC-2 10 x 10 lookout ground house constructed in 1933. Conflicts with the 1934 date in the register and firelookout.com.
Panorama photographs dated 26 August 1933, captioned as the Bear Bones Mountain lookout (register); taken by William Birchall (Forest Lookouts)
Register: built in 1934 as an L-5 ground cabin. firelookout.com: 1934 L-6 cab.
C. A. Paddock sent to the lookout as emergency lookout fireman (Eugene Register-Guard item, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Coast and Geodetic Survey station described on the summit; the description refers to the lookout house and a disk stamped BEARBONES 1953
Gone by 1964 (register); 'Gone 1964' (firelookout.com). Method of removal not stated.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say 1934; Forest Lookouts gives a plan FC-2 house built in 1933, and a panorama dated 26 August 1933 is captioned as the lookout. The sources do not settle the year, so the story gives both.
The register says an L-5 ground cabin, firelookout.com says an L-6 cab, and Forest Lookouts says a plan FC-2 10 x 10 ground house. The story reports all three.
firelookout.com says 14 miles south of Oakridge; the 1953 survey text says about 15 miles. Minor difference, reported as a range in the story's wording.

notes_for_editor: Three sources, all read; none describes the site today. Spelling varies (Bear Bones, Bearbones). The record's material 'wood' is not stated by any source we read; left unchanged. A Willamette National Forest lookout history (a scholarsbank thesis) appeared in search results but was not read; it may give a removal date and the design. Staffing evidence is a single 1935 item.
